brief: GS forecasts September nonfarm payrolls rose 80k, slightly below the 88k consensus but above the 71k three-month average. It forecasts private payrolls at 75k versus an 80k consensus. Arguing for a stronger print: initial jobless claims averaged 204k in the September payroll month, in line with August. The JOLTS layoff rate fell 0.1pp to 1.0% in August. Challenger layoffs fell 2k to 52k in September. Alternative big-data measures averaged 77k, up from August's 31k, though still slightly below consensus. Arguing for a weaker print: Labor Day fell late this year, on September 7th, and in past years with a similarly late Labor Day, September payroll growth has underperformed its recent trend. August's strength is also viewed as overstated: rebounds in local education and leisure and hospitality payrolls added a combined 104k, a swing GS does not expect to repeat. GS forecasts the unemployment rate edged down to 4.0% from a prior forecast and reading of 4.1%, on declining continuing claims, and average hourly earnings up 0.2% month over month, below the 0.3% consensus, on negative calendar effects. GS's slack tracker stands at 4.6%, suggesting the labor market is somewhat softer than the unemployment rate alone implies.
